questions.q: At very long context lengths, what typically becomes the dominant constraint on GPU memory?
options: The size of the model's weights
The KV cache, which scales linearly with sequence length for every concurrent request
The size of the tokenizer vocabulary
The number of attention heads defined in the architecture
questions.explain: Because KV cache size scales linearly with sequence length per request, a single long-context request's cache alone can consume gigabytes — making cache size, not model weight size, the dominant memory cost at long context.

questions.q: Why does attention compute become a bottleneck specifically at very long context?
options: Attention compute is constant regardless of sequence length
Standard attention compute grows quadratically with sequence length, since every token's query attends every other token's key
Attention compute only matters during decode, never during prefill
Longer context always reduces the compute required for attention
questions.explain: Standard attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length. A prompt 10x longer needs roughly 100x the attention compute for that portion of the forward pass, which starts to dominate prefill time at extreme lengths.

questions.q: Why is chunked prefill described as essential, not just helpful, at long context?
options: Because a very long prompt's prefill, run as one uninterrupted step, would stall every other request on the GPU for a long time
Because chunked prefill eliminates the need for a KV cache at long context
Because long prompts cannot be processed without chunked prefill under any circumstances
Because chunked prefill only applies to requests shorter than 1,000 tokens
questions.explain: At long context, an uninterrupted prefill for a very long prompt could stall other in-flight requests for a long time, making chunking into interleaved pieces load-bearing rather than merely beneficial.

questions.q: What does KV cache offloading do when a cache grows too large for GPU memory?
options: It deletes the oldest tokens from the conversation permanently
It moves colder, less-recently-used portions of the cache to CPU memory or fast local storage, paging them back in when needed
It automatically reduces the model's parameter count
It refuses to process any further requests from that user
questions.explain: KV cache offloading trades some latency for the ability to serve a request at all, by moving less-recently-used cache portions off the GPU to CPU memory or storage and paging them back in on demand.

questions.q: Why are this chapter's techniques (GQA/MQA, PagedAttention, prompt caching, chunked prefill, cache quantization) described as compounding rather than substituting for each other at long context?
options: Because only one of these techniques can ever be active at a time

Because each technique addresses a different part of the same cost — shrinking per-token cache size, eliminating fragmentation, avoiding recomputation, and preventing one request from starving others — and all of them are needed together as context grows
Because long context eliminates the need for any of these techniques
Because they are all identical techniques with different names
questions.explain: Long context amplifies cost on multiple fronts simultaneously, so GQA/MQA, PagedAttention, prompt caching, chunked prefill, and cache quantization each address a distinct part of the problem and stack together rather than replacing one another.
